Apple occasionally shares real-life stories of users being saved thanks to Apple Watch safety features.

Today, Apple released a new video about how Fall Detection and Emergency SOS helped rescue an injured cyclist. You can watch it below.

Apple showcases Apple Watch safety features

In a new video on its YouTube channel, Apple tells the story of Phil, who crashed while mountain biking with his children and lost consciousness on the spot.

In a video commissioned by Apple, Phil says he "miscalculated" a jump, breaking his collarbone and seven ribs. The impact knocked him out, but his Apple Watch automatically called emergency services and shared his location, allowing firefighters to find him and get him to hospital, where he recovered for a week.

Watch the video below:

This video comes nearly a year after Apple aired a longer feature during last October's "Awe Dropping" event, which invited several Apple Watch users to share how the device helped them through medical emergencies, accidents and other life-threatening situations.

The video also follows Apple's earlier "Glad I Had It On" campaign in China this year, which featured three users sharing how Fall Detection, Crash Detection and heart rate alerts helped them in emergencies.
